# The literal instance-noun / dialect vocabulary for this crate's own purity self-test
# (`tests/no_plane_names.rs`). Kept OUTSIDE the crate's `.rs` tree on purpose: this data's
# entire job is to spell, verbatim, the words the neighbouring `instance-noun-neutrality`
# gate forbids everywhere else in this crate — the test cannot do its job without holding
# them somewhere. Moving them into a non-`.rs` fixture (the gate walks `.rs` under
# `crates/` only) drains the noun census to zero for `no_plane_names.rs` without changing
# a single assertion, a single word, or a single byte of behaviour: it is the same
# structural move that already exempts the gate's own source (`xtask/src/gates/
# instance_noun_neutrality.rs`, which must also spell every noun) — that file is exempt by
# living outside `crates/`; this file is exempt the same way.
#
# Format: `[section]` header, then `key=value` lines (a bare line under `[plane_crates]` is
# itself the datum — nothing in the .rs file needs to name an individual plane-crate entry).

[plane_crates]
busbar-plane-
busbar_plane_
busbar-llm
busbar_llm
busbar-mcp
busbar_mcp
busbar-a2a
busbar_a2a
busbar-voice
busbar_voice

[dialect_words]
DIALECT_1=a2a
DIALECT_2=mcp
DIALECT_3=llm
DIALECT_4=voice
DIALECT_5=jsonrpc
DIALECT_6=json-rpc

[entries]
NEEDLE_1_HAYSTACK=let x = A2A_MOUNT;
NEEDLE_1_BARE=A2A_MOUNT
NEEDLE_1_SUBSTR=A2A
NEEDLE_2_HAYSTACK=this is the a2a binding
NEEDLE_3_HAYSTACK=the MCP door
NEEDLE_4_HAYSTACK=dialect: voice
NEEDLE_5_HAYSTACK=a json-rpc envelope
NEG_1_HAYSTACK=the authority is voiceless
NEG_2_HAYSTACK=0xa2a1 is a number
PLANE_LINE=busbar-plane-a2a = { path = "../busbar-plane-a2a" }
